scanner_doubts: lqramsey.md, lines 472, 481, 513 - qe-math-010 (proposed) is reported as 11 but should be at least 14: `\mathbb E_t` on these three lines is the same 'missing braces' defect as the 11 that were caught, and it is missed because of a word-boundary bug in check_math_010 (tools/qestyle_rules.py:547). The pattern is `\\(?:mathbb|Bbb)\s+[PEV]\b`, and `\b` cannot match between `E` and `_` since `_` is a word character - so `\mathbb E` is caught and `\mathbb E_t` is not. Replacing `\b` with `(?![A-Za-z])` fixes it. Corpus-wide, `\\(mathbb|Bbb)[[:space:]]+[PEV]_` matches 98 lines across the five series (44 in lecture-dp). Separately, the bare `E_t` at 497, 505, 547 (twice) and 562 is the expectation operator written with no blackboard at all; the rule's bare-letter branch requires the letter to be applied to a bracketed argument (`E[`, `E\{`, `E(`), so `E_t \sum` and `E_t p^t_{t+1}` fall outside it. Whether that branch should also fire on a bare `E_t` followed by a `\sum` or a symbol is a rule-scope decision worth making once.

lqramsey.md, lines 401 and 430 - qe-math-002 is reported as 8 but only 6 transposes exist. Every prime in this file is a genuine transpose; the two extras are double counts of `x_t'`, matched once by the `prime` branch of check_math_002 and again by `prime_vec` catching the `t'` inside the subscripted symbol, because the lookbehind at tools/qestyle_rules.py:393 does not exclude `_`. Same defect as reported against lq_inventories, lagrangian_lqdp and markov_jump_lq; 74 lines in lecture-dp are affected.

lqramsey.md, lines 787, 788, 789, 794, 795, 796, 801, 806, 807, 808, 833, 840 - all 12 qe-fig-008 hits are false positives. Every one of these `plot` calls ends in `**p_args`, and `p_args = {'lw': 2, 'alpha': 0.7}` is defined at 783 for `gen_fig_1` and 829 for `gen_fig_2`, so the line width the rule asks for is already 2. check_fig_008 (tools/qestyle_rules.py) assembles the call's argument text and then searches it for a literal `lw=` or `linewidth=`, which a splatted dictionary does not contain. The fix is to treat a `**name` argument as unknown rather than as absent - either skip the call, or resolve `name` against a dict literal assigned earlier in the same cell. Scope: within lecture-dp only lqramsey.md and lqcontrol.md use this idiom (lqcontrol has 8 such plot calls), but both are in my assignment and in both the rule accounts for most of the Figures deduction.
